title: How rogue officers turned a nationwide camera network into a tool for stalking

reports.title: Kechi police lieutenant arrested for using police technology to stalk wife
Former Kechi police lieutenant convicted on stalking charges
A former police officer has been sentenced in Sedgwick County District Court
‘You were spotted’: KS officer who used police cameras to stalk estranged wife sentenced
Wichita moves to tighten access, increase oversight on secretive police surveillance program
How rogue officers turned a nationwide camera network into a tool for stalking

summary:
Kechi Police Lieutenant Victor Heiar was arrested by Wichita police after he allegedly used the Wichita Police Department's Flock license plate reader technology to track his estranged wife's location. He has been removed from his department and booked into Sedgwick County Jail on one count of stalking and one count of unlawful acts concerning computers.

The article notes that Wichita and Sedgwick County law enforcement recently received $1.6 million in federal funds for license plate readers and upgraded camera technology. Defense attorney Charles O'Hara said officers must not use secret information for personal use, while private investigator Joseph Schillaci called the incident isolated and not a common problem. The article does not state any upcoming court dates or further steps in Heiar's case.
